title: How Silane Surface Modification Affects the Structure of PLA/Wax/ZnO Composites During Hydrolytic Degradation
content: The production and use of petroleum-derived plastics, which do not decompose easily in the environment, have led to significant environmental problems and contributed to global warming [1]. Plastic pollution is a widespread issue that persists from production to disposal [2]. In response to these challenges, polymer derived from natural sources are emerging as viable alternatives to conventional plastics due to their enhanced properties and applications. However, non-biodegradable bioplastics also present concerns, such as the generation of microplastics and slow degradation rates. AS a result, research has focused on blending and compatibilizing various natural polymers and biological additives to achieve optimal performance, balancing biodegradability and functionality.
